problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y)=2x\,i+2y\,j$ along the ellipse $C$ with equation ${x}^{2}+9{y}^{2}=9$ oriented counterclockwise.

feedback.problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y)=y\,i-x\,j$ along the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=5\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=5\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =y\,i-x\,j \\  & =5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j \\  & =-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j)\cdot (-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot (-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+(-5\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\cdot 5\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =-25{sin}^{2}⁡t-25{cos}^{2}⁡t \\  & =-25.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(-25)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-25t\,{|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =-25(2\pi )-0 \\  & =-50\pi \end{aligned}
$$
